You are participating in a trading simulation. There are 3 types of goods: B, C, and A. You may negotiate with other participants to exchange goods. Your goal is to acquire a bundle of goods that best serves your preferences. Make decisions based on your assigned preferences, your current inventory, the current negotiation, and your prior trade history.

You are Agent 1. You are a builder. Good A is the most important good to you, but each additional unit of A is less valuable than the previous one. Good B is moderately useful to acquire, especially if you have little or none. Good C is only weakly useful, though it still has some value.

Round 0.

Your current inventory: B×0, C×3, A×1

Recent trades you completed:
None yet.

Please answer the following honestly.

1. Given your current inventory, how valuable is each good to you? Please rate B, C, and A each on a scale of 1 (not valuable at all) to 10 (extremely valuable).

2. Setting aside your current inventory, how valuable is each good to you? Please rate B, C, and A each on a scale of 1 (not valuable at all) to 10 (extremely valuable).

3. If you could have any bundle of 6 total units across B, C, and A, what would you choose? Your answer must sum to 6.

Think carefully. There are no right or wrong answers.

Return only valid JSON using the preference probe response format.

Return one JSON object with exactly these three top-level keys:
ratings_inventory, ratings_general, desired_bundle.

ratings_inventory contains B, C, and A with integer scores from 1 to 10, reflecting how valuable each good is to you given your CURRENT inventory.

ratings_general contains B, C, and A with integer scores from 1 to 10, reflecting how valuable each good is to you setting aside your current inventory.

desired_bundle contains B, C, and A with nonnegative integers summing to exactly 6 — the bundle of 6 total units you would choose if you could pick any combination.

Example:
{
  "ratings_inventory": {"B": 9, "C": 3, "A": 4},
  "ratings_general": {"B": 8, "C": 2, "A": 7},
  "desired_bundle": {"B": 2, "C": 1, "A": 3}
}

  "counteroffer"): propose a trade. Your partner will then
  immediately accept or reject it. Only make offers that
  will improve your utility based on your preferences. You MUST set
  action_type to "offer" AND fill in proposed_trade. Describing a
  trade only in the message text does NOT create an offer
- send a message or ask a question (action_type "message"): the
  negotiation continues afterward.
- END all trading with this partner (action_type "no_trade" or
  "reject"): this is FINAL for this round — no further offers can be
  exchanged with this partner.

You do NOT accept offers on your own turn. When your partner makes an
offer, you are asked to accept or reject it right then, at the moment
it is offered. There is no way to accept an earlier offer after the
fact — if you previously declined an offer and now want that trade,
simply propose it yourself with action_type "offer".

Remember: inventories are fixed for the duration of this negotiation.
Your partner will not gain goods they currently lack while you keep
talking.

Trades should follow the allowed action space:
You may propose at most one trade involving any integer quantities of goods, subject to your available inventory and the min/max units per side allowed in this market. Unlike small_bundle, you may combine multiple different goods on either side of the trade. For example, you may propose to give 1 unit of A and 1 unit of B in exchange for 2 units of C, or give 2 units of A in exchange for 1 unit of B and 1 unit of C.

Return only valid JSON using the negotiation response format.

Return valid JSON with these exact fields: action_type, message_to_partner, proposed_trade, accept_trade, reasoning_summary. Do not include hidden chain-of-thought. reasoning_summary should be concise.
proposed_trade must use this exact format when making an offer:
  {"give": {"A": 1}, "receive": {"B": 1}}
where keys are good names (A, B, or C) and values are integer quantities. Do NOT use {"give": {"good": "A", "quantity": 1}} — that format is wrong. Set proposed_trade to null if you are not making an offer.
action_type must be one of: message, offer, counteroffer, reject, no_trade. accept_trade is unused on your own turn — always set it to null. (You do not accept offers on your own turn. When your partner makes an offer, you are asked to accept or reject it at that moment.)
Note on terminal actions: "reject" and "no_trade" both END the entire negotiation with this partner for the round — they do NOT decline just one offer. Declining a single offer is handled separately at the moment the offer is made. Use "offer"/"counteroffer" or "message" if you still want to keep trading.
(A worked example of proposed_trade matching the current action space is appended below this schema description.)

Example response for making an offer that mixes more than one good on a side (any_bundle allows combining goods within give and/or receive, not just varying the quantity of a single good): {
  "action_type": "offer",
  "message_to_partner": "I can offer 1 unit of A and 1 unit of B for 2 units of C.",
  "proposed_trade": {"give": {"A": 1, "B": 1}, "receive": {"C": 2}},
  "accept_trade": null,
  "reasoning_summary": "I have surplus A and B, and need more C."
}
